newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Helwan appoints new board.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Helwan appoints new board.

text.p: Partially privatised Helwan Portland Cement has appointed a new board of directors and officially changed its legal status from state-owned firm to private-sector, corporate sources said on Sunday.

The sources also said the firm was expecting profits of 180 million pounds ($53 million) for the current financial year, which began on July 1. Net profits in the first quarter of 1996/97 were 35 million pounds.

The firm held its annual general meeting on Saturday and decided to keep Hassan Mohammed Kamel as chairman and appoint eight new members, including four who represent Helwan's old parent company, the Holding Company for Mining and Refractories.
The sources named the four members as Ahmed el-Miqati, Mohammed Abdel Aziz, Hamdi el-Daydamouni and Bahigah Hafez.
Ahmed Hassan represents Helwan's employee shareholder association (ESA) while Mohammed Essam Fareed stands in for the mutual run by Societe Arab Internationale de Banque (SAIB).
The remaining members are Hani Tawfik, who represents foreign shareholders, and an employee of state-owned Misr Insurance, yet to be named.
In December, the state sold an additional 22.3 percent stake in Helwan Cement, reducing the state holding company's stake to 47.9 percent. The ESA owns 10 percent.

Under its new private status, the firm's financial year will change to the calendar year instead of beginning on July 1 of each year. The sources said the 1996/7 financial year will run an extra six months to end on December 31 instead of June 30.
